## Natural history notes

A small running crab spider characterized by a flattened body, long laterally spread legs, and mottled tan, gray, or brown coloration that helps it blend against bark, leaves, and stems. In Florida, Philodromus floridensis is part of the state’s spider fauna and is most likely found in warm wooded or semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, pine flatwoods, shrubs, gardens, and tree trunks. It is an active ambush-and-pursuit predator, moving quickly over vegetation or bark to capture small insects and other arthropods, while using silk mainly for retreats and egg sacs rather than prey-capture webs.
